mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 728i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 7 Series 728i engine replacement typically costs £1,200-£2,000 for a used M52B28 unit, £2,200-£3,200 for a reconditioned engine, and £2,800-£3,800 for a fully rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit costs add approximately £700-£1,000 depending on your location and the specialist's labour rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M52 engine failure in a BMW 7 Series 728i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of M52 engine trouble in a 728i include: overheating or coolant loss (cooling system failure), rough idling or loss of low-end power (VANOS issues on M52TUB28), rattling noise from the front of the engine (timing chain tensioner), oil spots under the car (valve cover or oil filter housing gasket leaks), and white smoke from the exhaust (head gasket failure after overheating).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 728i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 7 Series 728i is otherwise in good condition, a replacement engine can extend its life significantly and retain the car's value. With a typical E38 728i valued at £3,000-£10,000 depending on condition, a rebuilt engine at £2,800-£3,800 plus fitting represents a sound investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 728i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 7 Series 728i engine replacements take 1-2 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 24-72 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 7 Series 728i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 7 Series 728i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier, and reconditioned engines often carry a 12-24 month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M52B28 and M52TUB28 in the BMW 7 Series 728i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M52B28 (1995-1998) is the earlier single-VANOS engine with 193hp. The M52TUB28 (1998-2001) is the technical update with dual VANOS, offering improved low-end torque and smoother power delivery. The M52TUB28 also has revised cylinder head and block castings with iron liners, addressing the Nikasil bore wear issues that affected some early M52 engines.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 7 Series 728i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 728i joined the E38 7 Series range in 1996 as the entry-level petrol model, complementing the range of V8 and V12 engines with a more economical straight-six option. Powered by the 2.8-litre M52 engine - familiar from the 328i and 528i - the 728i became one of the most successful models in the E38 line-up, offering a refined driving experience in a luxury saloon. The 728i was produced across both pre-facelift and facelift E38 generations, with the engine receiving a technical update in 1998.

milestones.description: M52B28, 2.8L naturally aspirated straight-six petrol, 193hp, launched as entry-level E38 728i and 728iL (long wheelbase)
Facelift (LCI) update across E38 range; M52TUB28 introduced with dual VANOS variable valve timing for improved low-end torque and refined power delivery
Facelift model 728i (193hp) continues production with revised styling
E38 production ends in July 2001; 728i nameplate retired

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 7 Series 728i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 728i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 7 Series 728i is powered by the M52B28 and M52TUB28 - 2.8-litre straight-six petrol engines that are generally robust and relatively inexpensive to repair compared to the V8 and V12 units in the E38 range. Replacement demand for the 728i is typically driven by cooling system failures, VANOS issues, and timing chain tensioner wear. Rebuilt BMW 7 Series 728i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 728i M52 Engine Suffers
problems.rootCause: The M52 engine is notorious for cooling system issues, particularly with plastic components that become brittle over time. The thermostat housing and water pump can crack and fail, leading to overheating and potential head gasket failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace thermostat, water pump, radiator, expansion tank, and hoses
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for preventative maintenance or early-stage failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace head gasket, skim head if warped
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if overheating has caused gasket failure but block is undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt engine with new cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if overheating has caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 7 Series 728i E38 is valued between £3,000 and £10,000 depending on condition, mileage and specification. For vehicles worth £5,000+, a rebuilt engine at £2,800-£3,800 plus fitting is financially viable. For cars at the lower end of the value spectrum (under £4,000), a used engine or scrappage may be the more sensible choice.
problems.recommendation: Cooling system preventative maintenance is the single most important thing you can do for your 728i. Replacing the thermostat, water pump, and expansion tank every 60,000 miles (£500-£800 at a specialist) is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. If your 728i has overheated, have the head gasket inspected immediately - catching it early can save the engine.

problems.h4: VANOS System Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 728i M52TUB28 Suffers
problems.rootCause: The dual VANOS system on the M52TUB28 can develop issues due to seal wear, leading to loss of oil pressure and improper camshaft timing. Symptoms include rough idling, loss of low-end power, poor fuel economy, and a rattling noise from the front of the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace VANOS seals with upgraded Viton seals
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early; restores timing and performance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, guides, and VANOS seals
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if timing chain rattle is also present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt engine with rebuilt VANOS, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if VANOS failure has caused timing chain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 1998-2001 BMW 7 Series 728i valued at £4,000-£8,000, a VANOS seal replacement at £400-£600 is a worthwhile investment. A full engine replacement remains viable for well-maintained examples worth £5,000+.
problems.recommendation: VANOS issues on the M52TUB28 are almost always caused by failed seals - replacing them with upgraded Viton seals (£400-£600 at a specialist) is a cost-effective fix that restores factory performance. If the VANOS rattle is accompanied by timing chain noise, have the entire timing system inspected; a full timing chain and VANOS overhaul (£900-£1,500) is still far cheaper than a replacement engine.
